literal: Making excessively (outwardly), those who despise themselves (inwardly), making (them) smile, within friendship, to embrace (them) to death is the proper way.
translation: With those who outwardly display excessive affection but inwardly despise you, it is fitting to make them smile with outward friendliness, yet embrace them to their ruin within that very friendship.
modern: வெளிப்படையாகப் பெரிதும் அன்பு காட்டி, மனத்திற்குள் நம்மை இகழ்பவர்களை, நாமும் முகமலர்ச்சி அடையச் செய்து, அந்த நட்பிற்குள்ளேயே அவர்களை அழிப்பதே தகுதியானது.
explanation: This couplet advises on how to deal with deceitful, feigned friends. The poet describes enemies who pretend to be highly affectionate ('mika ceytu') but secretly hold contempt ('tam eḷḷuvārai'). The strategy to counter them is to reciprocate their behavior: make them smile outwardly ('naka ceytu') while maintaining the guise of friendship ('naṭpiṉuḷ'), but ultimately deliver a fatal blow or neutralize them ('cā pullal' - embracing to death or ruin). It emphasizes that deceit must be met with strategic, protective deceit to ensure one's own survival.
